title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This act seeks to protect election integrity by preventing and detecting AI-generated misinformation that could influence voters. It establishes guidelines for election officials, imposes penalties for deceptive AI use, and promotes transparency in campaign communications.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House urges Congress to refuse extra funding or special regulatory help for companies or banks facing collapse due to stress in the AI market and instead direct resources toward Americans who have been harmed. This approach prioritizes protecting consumers over providing bailouts to affected AI-related firms.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes federal standards to ensure AI research is reliable, safe, and transparent. It requires researchers to conduct rigorous testing, disclose methods and results, and adhere to accountability guidelines to protect public interest.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 seeks to make the Department of Veterans Affairs’ use of artificial intelligence clearer and more accountable. It likely requires the VA to disclose how AI systems are deployed, their decision‑making logic, and to adhere to federal standards for safety, privacy, and bias mitigation.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to ensure that artificial intelligence used in evaluating and processing veterans' claims operates transparently, fairly, and responsibly. The law establishes oversight, requires clear documentation of AI decision‑making, and imposes accountability standards to protect veterans' rights and prevent bias in claim determinations.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard people by requiring AI companies to be clear, honest, and accountable in how they present and market their products. It establishes rules for labeling, disclosure, and enforcement so consumers can trust that AI services aren’t misleading or harmful.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is intended to set national standards and guidelines for the secure development and deployment of AI systems. It seeks to create a framework that identifies, assesses, mitigates, and monitors AI-related security risks to protect public safety and national interests.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a national task force to safeguard artificial intelligence systems that support critical infrastructure. It outlines responsibilities for developing security standards, monitoring threats, and fostering collaboration among government, industry, and academia to protect AI‑driven assets.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes rules to identify, evaluate, and mitigate the risks that AI systems may pose, requiring developers and users to implement safety measures and report potential hazards. It creates oversight mechanisms, compliance standards, and penalties aimed at protecting public safety and privacy while promoting responsible AI innovation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 sets rules for how AI‑driven machines like drones, autonomous cars, and robotic systems should work together safely. It establishes standards for safety, accountability, and interoperability so that these physical AI systems can operate responsibly in shared air and ground environments.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to stop AI-generated content from misleading voters and skewing election outcomes. It sets rules requiring disclosure, oversight, and accountability for any AI tools used in political campaigning or election-related communications.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires that all AI systems capable of modifying themselves be continuously overseen by regulators. It mandates that developers submit regular safety reports, keep detailed logs of any self‑changes, and obtain approval before deploying autonomous updates.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law aimed at preventing artificial intelligence systems from acting independently or unpredictably. It seeks to establish regulatory safeguards, oversight mechanisms, and limits on the deployment of AI technologies that pose risks to public safety or security.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act proposes a pause on building and running new data centers that are dedicated to artificial intelligence. The goal is to give lawmakers time to study the environmental, economic, and societal impacts before allowing further development.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to investigate and oversee cybersecurity incidents involving AI systems. It aims to improve transparency, set industry standards, and hold AI developers and users accountable for security failures.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is intended to guide the development and use of artificial intelligence so that it benefits everyday people in the United States. It establishes rules, oversight, and funding to promote safe, fair, and accessible AI that supports jobs, innovation, and public well‑being.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies and research institutions to regularly submit detailed reports on their AI systems, including performance metrics, resource consumption, and potential societal impacts. This law aims to increase transparency, ensure accountability, and help the government monitor and guide the development of artificial intelligence within the country.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 mandates that all medical diagnoses and treatments be conducted by licensed human doctors, not by artificial‑intelligence systems. It limits AI’s role in healthcare to supportive tools only, ensuring accountability and patient safety by keeping decision‑making in human hands.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy creates a new office inside the President’s Executive Office that will focus on spotting and dealing with dangers from artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. It outlines the office’s duties, how it will work with other agencies, and its authority to develop strategies to protect national security and public interests.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee and guide AI development, ensuring its responsible and ethical use. The committee will investigate AI-related issues, recommend policies and regulations, and promote best practices for AI technologies.
